findings.title: Sharded queries are interpolated twice
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery applies template variables to each target before passing them to splitQueriesByStreamShard. That code later calls runSplitQuery, and runSplitQuery now unconditionally applies template variables again to request.targets. As a result, already-interpolated queries, including ones that have had shard selectors injected, are interpolated a second time. Template interpolation is not guaranteed to be idempotent: variable values that contain template syntax, ad-hoc filter placeholders, or other variable-like text can be expanded or modified again, producing incorrect LogQL queries or duplicated filters. It also adds unnecessary work for every shard/time-split subrequest.

findings.title: Empty queries produced by interpolation are not filtered
findings.body: runSplitQuery filters targets on query.expr before calling applyTemplateVariables, but it does not filter again after interpolation. If a raw expression is a non-empty variable such as `$selector` and interpolation resolves it to an empty string, the target remains in the query list and can be grouped and sent to Loki as an empty expression. This can create unnecessary or failing subrequests. The mapped queries should be filtered again after interpolation.

findings.title: Step-splitting test uses the wrong request object and mutates shared state
findings.body: The test creates `req` as a shallow copy of `request`, sets `req.targets[0].step = '10s'`, but then calls `runSplitQuery(datasource, request)` instead of `runSplitQuery(datasource, req)`. It only passes because the shallow copy shares the same targets array/object, so the mutation leaks into the shared outer `request`. This makes the test order-dependent and can affect later tests. It should use the intended request object and avoid mutating shared test state.
